title: Deutschland First: What the rise of the AfD means for Europe – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: ECFR scenario paper (explicitly not a prediction) modelling a 2029 Bundestag based on late-2026 polling: AfD largest with 200 seats, forcing a fragile CDU/CSU-SPD-Green 'Kenya coalition'. The authors argue the AfD need not govern to transform Germany: stagnation, deindustrialisation and volatility already make Berlin more inward-looking, keener to pay less into the EU, favour its own industry and rearm nationally, so Europe should keep Germany engaged while building coalitions able to act without it.

themes.theme: 2029 Bundestag scenario and the strained firewall

insights.claim: ECFR's scenario, built exactly on the late-2026 polling average, has the AfD winning 200 Bundestag seats in 2029 versus 145 for the CDU/CSU, 110 Greens, 98 SPD and 77 Left, the first time since 1945 a far-right party would be strongest in parliament.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Benchmark for German political-risk pricing; Bund spreads/yields could react to an AfD-largest outcome.
insights.locator: The far-right Alternative for Germany party

insights.claim: With the AfD largest and the CDU/CSU too weak for a minority government, the only remaining option would be a 'Kenya coalition' of CDU/CSU, SPD and Greens, ideologically broader than Scholz's collapsed traffic-light coalition and born of necessity rather than shared vision, making budgets especially hard to pass.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Expect chronic German fiscal-policy gridlock and budget delays; negative for policy predictability.

insights.claim: The CDU/CSU and SPD together won just 45% of the vote in the February 2025 snap election (328 seats, majority of 12), versus 69% and 448 seats when Merkel took office in 2005.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Structural erosion of the centre, not a cyclical dip.

insights.claim: The AfD has risen from 10.3% in the 2021 federal election to second-largest party in the Bundestag and leading the polls; an April 2025 poll first showed it ahead on 25%, one point above the CDU.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Sustained AfD momentum raises odds of firewall erosion over the decade.

insights.claim: The firewall is weakening: in January 2025 a CDU/CSU migration motion passed with AfD support, and in October 2026 several Saxony-Anhalt CDU politicians appeared to back the AfD candidate for parliamentary speaker; state-level case-by-case cooperation would pressure the federal CDU right to follow.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: State-level breaches in the east are leading indicators of federal firewall collapse.
insights.locator: Signs of the pressure the firewall

insights.claim: Beyond migration, the CDU/CSU right and AfD could find common ground on tax cuts, deregulation, curbing EU costs and rules, anti-'wokeism' and support for German rearmament, despite deep differences on rule of law and Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: A CDU-AfD policy convergence would push Germany toward deregulation and EU-budget restraint.

insights.claim: A Chancellor Weidel remains a distant prospect, since four in five German voters live in western states where AfD support is around a quarter, so nationally it needs the CDU/CSU to split or change course to govern.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: AfD-led government risk is low this decade; the bigger risk is influence from opposition.
insights.quote: A Chancellor Weidel thus remains a distant prospect.

insights.claim: Germany is by some estimates losing about 15,000 industrial jobs a month, and one Volkswagen leak suggested several production sites could close with up to 100,000 job losses.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Negative read-across for German autos, suppliers and the Mittelstand; supports AfD protest vote.
insights.quote: losing about 15,000 industrial jobs a month
insights.locator: In October 2026, the German and French

insights.claim: Germany's economy has stagnated since 2019, and even Merz's March 2025 debt-brake reform to borrow for infrastructure and defence has generated only a modest growth uptick, estimated at 1.2% for 2026, with private consumption subdued as households save.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Fiscal stimulus is not yet translating into strong growth; watch consumption and savings rate.
insights.locator: Germany failed to use its boom years

insights.claim: A 'second China shock' is hitting Germany as China moves up the value chain with aggressive currency and subsidy policies, generating a glut of high-value goods like cars and making brands such as BYD global EV leaders.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Structural headwind for German carmakers; tailwind for Chinese EV exporters; trade-defence risk rises.
insights.locator: The country is also deindustrialising rapidly

insights.claim: In October 2026 Germany and France proposed a 'last resort' mechanism letting the European Commission restrict single-market access for companies from countries using economic coercion against the EU, implicitly targeting China, though it may come too late for German industry.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Watch for EU anti-coercion measures hitting Chinese firms; risk of retaliation on EU exporters.
insights.locator: In October 2026, the German and French

insights.claim: Polling in September 2026 found half of Germans worried about their standard of living, and 86% of Saxony-Anhalt voters who switched from CDU to AfD cited disappointment with politicians unable to solve the country's problems.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Economic anxiety is the main driver of AfD gains; economic recovery is the key swing factor.

insights.claim: A senior AfD politician invoked a 'pocketbook theory': Germans tolerated EU membership costs in good times but economic doubts are prompting them to question the European status quo.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Prolonged stagnation could erode Germany's pro-EU consensus and support for fiscal transfers.
insights.locator: The far right will likely aim to exploit

insights.claim: Weidel has consolidated power through 'professionalisation without moderation', a pact with extremist-wing leader Björn Höcke, and strategic ambiguity such as backtracking within days on calls to leave Schengen and the euro zone.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: AfD euro-exit rhetoric is a recurring tail-risk headline; watch for it near elections.

insights.claim: The AfD's main split is east versus west: eastern branches are more statist, more extreme on migration, more hostile to Westbindung and open to multipolar order, while western voters are more bourgeois and attached to the Western alliance.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: AfD foreign policy direction depends on which wing dominates; Russia policy risk sits with the east.

insights.claim: The AfD's EU plan remains radical: abolish the European Parliament, disempower the Commission, scrap Green Deal legislation, and use Germany's veto on the EU budget as blackmail to force these changes.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Any AfD leverage over German EU-budget votes threatens EU fiscal capacity and climate policy.
insights.quote: it plans to use Germany’s veto against the EU budget as blackmail
insights.locator: But Germany’s departure from the EU

insights.claim: In the Saxony-Anhalt parliament the AfD's first proposal was a Bundesrat initiative to end sanctions against, and normalise relations with, Russia, showing how state-level power could translate into Bundesrat leverage.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: State wins give AfD a channel to pressure Russia sanctions policy.

insights.claim: The AfD need not be in power to transform Germany: volatility, stagnation and the AfD's mere presence are already making Berlin more inward-looking and less willing to compromise in Brussels.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Lower probability of German-enabled EU fiscal integration (joint debt, larger budgets).
insights.quote: the AfD does not need to be in power to transform Germany

insights.claim: Merz declared in July 2026 that European integration was 'at its limits', blamed EU red tape and green policies for Germany's woes, and is demanding a drastic cut to the proposed next EU long-term budget, beyond the Irish presidency's October 2026 compromise.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: German resistance points to a smaller MFF; negative for EU-funded programmes and net-recipient states.

insights.claim: A changed Germany would remain in the EU but want to pay less, demand more in return and favour its own industry, including pushing for renationalised competition policy that loosens national-subsidy rules where its fiscal space advantages German firms.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Expect German state aid to distort the single market; relative winner German champions, losers fiscally weaker states.
insights.quote: The changed Germany would want to pay less into the EU, demand more in return and favour its own industry.

insights.claim: A Kenya coalition with a rebellious CDU/CSU right and portfolios split across four parties would mean the 'German vote' (Berlin abstaining for lack of coalition agreement) 'on steroids', while an AfD blocking minority, possibly with the BSW, could veto further EU integration steps.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Fewer EU decisions requiring German two-thirds votes; slower EU legislation.
insights.locator: But a sense of existential danger

insights.claim: Paradoxically, a disengaged Germany may become more heavy-handed in the EU, using intergovernmental 'union method' leverage while no longer accepting upfront sovereignty or cash costs for long-term integration.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Germany as a more demanding, transactional partner changes EU crisis-response odds.
insights.quote: Paradoxically, a disengaged Germany may also feel more heavy-handed within the EU.

insights.claim: Germany has historically been Europe's crisis manager of last resort (euro zone, NextGenerationEU common debt, Ukraine), and weaker governments plus a rising AfD shrink the room for such big German compromises.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Reduced likelihood of a German backstop in the next EU crisis; higher tail risk for periphery spreads.

insights.claim: The pressure to stress German interests extends even to the SPD: finance minister Lars Klingbeil shifted from resisting UniCredit's Commerzbank takeover to seeking guarantees for its German operations.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Cross-border bank M&A in Germany faces political conditions; relevant to UniCredit/Commerzbank.
insights.locator: And yet, when the AfD presents

insights.claim: The 2026 collapse of the Future Combat Air System fighter-jet project exemplifies narrow domestic industrial considerations in France and Germany trumping shared European defence.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Fragmented European defence procurement favours national champions over pan-European programmes.
insights.locator: A redefinition of the German interest

insights.claim: Current projections have Germany spending €152bn on defence by 2029, around 3.5% of GDP and roughly equal to Britain and France combined, making it Europe's biggest military power by some distance.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Large, sustained demand for German defence contractors through the decade.
insights.locator: A massive rise in defence spending

insights.claim: To legitimise high defence spending, a fragile coalition would frame it as industrial policy, incentivising procurement only from German companies to offset declines in sectors like autos, as foreshadowed by foreign minister Wadephul urging Ukraine to buy more German weapons.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Favours German defence primes over European/US suppliers in German procurement.
insights.quote: a strong political interest in framing defence spending as industrial policy

insights.claim: The AfD backs a strong Bundeswehr but attacks debt-financed defence spending as a burden on future generations, which undermines the foundations of German rearmament because its goals cannot be met without a massive rise in national debt.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Watch AfD leverage on defence borrowing as a risk to German defence budgets and Bund supply.
insights.locator: The AfD claims to want a strong Bundeswehr

insights.claim: A ceasefire or peace deal in Ukraine would likely trigger a German row over whether 3.5% defence spending remains necessary long term, shifting the debate from whether to rearm to sustainability and who the money protects.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Ceasefire headlines are a downside risk for German defence-spending expectations.
insights.locator: Were a ceasefire or peace agreement

insights.claim: The AfD supports NATO membership for now but wants it limited to territorial defence and ultimately favours an independent European military alliance outside EU and NATO, reinforcing a more transactional German view of alliances.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Transactional German alliance politics complicate eastern-flank commitments.

themes.theme: Russia policy and Ukraine support under pressure

insights.claim: A return to the pre-2022 Germany-Russia relationship is highly unlikely: the EU agreed in January 2026 to permanently ban all Russian gas imports by September 2027, so restoring Nord Stream as the AfD wants would require a Commission initiative and qualified majority, feasible only within a wider peace settlement.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Russian gas return to Europe is a low-probability tail; supportive for LNG supply contracts into Germany.
insights.quote: A return to the pre-2022 relationship with Russia is highly unlikely.

insights.claim: German industrial giants are unlikely to revive Russian business after massive post-2022 losses and Kremlin nationalisations, such as Volkswagen losing its billion-euro Kaluga factory.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Don't expect German corporate re-entry into Russia even in a peace scenario.

insights.claim: A potential US-Russia deal over Europeans' heads, with partial US military exit and withdrawal of Ukraine support, plus awareness of Bundeswehr weakness, could push Germany toward 'coming to an arrangement' with Russia more than any wish to renew the strategic partnership.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: US retrenchment is the key trigger for a softer German Russia line.

insights.claim: Political space exists for a more conciliatory Russia policy in the CDU's east and CSU (e.g. Saxony's Michael Kretschmer favouring post-ceasefire energy cooperation) and in the SPD's Ostpolitik tradition, while the Greens would be the most consistent opponents of reducing Ukraine support.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Coalition composition determines German Ukraine-support durability.
insights.locator: The coalition parties may not be universally

insights.claim: In ECFR's illustrative scenario, German Ukraine transfers fall from €11.6bn in 2026 to €7bn by 2031 with officials mulling cuts of up to half, and a constitutional court ruling requiring a two-thirds Bundestag majority gives the AfD a veto over Ukraine's EU accession.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Shows how a two-thirds requirement could become a hard block on Ukraine's EU accession.

themes.theme: How Europe should adapt to a different Germany

insights.claim: European governments should keep Berlin on board where possible but become adept at building coalitions to act without it, which could even improve the EU's ability to get things done.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Expect more enhanced-cooperation and coalition-of-the-willing EU initiatives.
insights.quote: must also become adept at building coalitions to act without it

insights.claim: The EU is already moving toward 'variable geometry', as with the €90bn Ukraine support loan agreed in December 2025 via enhanced cooperation to circumvent the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia; a Germany unable to agree joint action would strengthen this logic on the Green Deal and Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Enhanced cooperation is a working tool for financing Ukraine despite vetoes.

insights.claim: The Franco-German engine has given way to broader formats such as the E3 on geopolitics, the Weimar Triangle on defence and the E6 on competitiveness, which suit an EU facing an uncertain Germany and a France that could see a President Le Pen by mid-2027.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Track minilateral formats as the venues for real EU decisions.
insights.locator: The EU must curb its over-reliance

insights.claim: Partners should frame joint investments around jobs and growth to make them palatable in Germany, and value ministers and the next Commission president who can sell European goals in Berlin, with an early test being whether German resistance to a larger EU budget and common defence can be overcome.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: EU budget and common defence fund negotiations are the near-term signal of German engagement.

insights.claim: If Europeans simply hedge against the demise of Germany's post-Zeitenwende orientation, that could become a self-fulfilling prophecy.
insights.speaker: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
insights.so_what: Reflexivity: market and policy hedging against Germany may accelerate the drift.
insights.quote: this could become a self-fulfilling prophecy

source_meta.author: Piotr Buras, Jeremy Cliffe, Angela Mehrer, Jana Puglierin
